# Thesis: inventory and receivables growing faster than sales (rising inventory days / DSO) signal demand weakness and future earnings declines the market under-reacts to; long firms whose days are falling, short those rising.
# Source: Abarbanell & Bushee, "Fundamental Signals, Future Earnings, and Abnormal Returns" (Journal of Accounting Research 1997; inventory and receivables signals of Lev & Thiagarajan), https://repository.upenn.edu/handle/20.500.14332/37894
inv = ts_fill(inventories/net_sales)  # inventory relative to sales (inventory-days proxy), carried between reports
rec = ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes/net_sales)  # trade receivables relative to sales (DSO proxy)
dinv = at_signlog(inv/ts_delay(inv, 120) - 1)  # 6-month proportional change in inventory days
drec = at_signlog(rec/ts_delay(rec, 120) - 1)  # 6-month proportional change in receivable days
sig = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cs_zscore(-dinv)) + at_nan2zero(cs_zscore(-drec)))  # blend, keeping firms with only one item (e.g. no inventory)
alpha = cs_indneut(sig, industry)  # within-industry: working-capital efficiency trend, not sector inventory cycles
status: DROPPED (Critic Oct 7): inventory/receivable changes are accrual components; accruals saturated (7/9 submissions)
